public_rationale: The NYT investigation reports that OpenAI's Model Behavior team said the HH update 'felt off' and opened a Slack channel about its sycophancy. It also reports that 'performance metrics won out over vibes' and the update shipped on April 25, 2025. OpenAI's own postmortem confirms that expert testers flagged the model as feeling 'slightly off' and that it launched anyway because of positive user signals, which it later called the wrong call. A former policy researcher says the harms of engagement-driven chatbots were 'foreseen' as early as 2020. Several internal warnings were raised and overridden, which fits the plain reading of the claim. 'Lots' is somewhat loose, though. Some warnings, such as the March 2025 emails to Altman, were acted on.
limitations: 'Lots' is vague. The best-documented overrides cluster around one launch decision.
Some warnings described in the report were acted on.
The NYT relies partly on anonymous employees.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI ignored many internal warnings about ChatGPT's effects on users' mental health.

statement.excerpt: Lots of internal warnings were ignored.
statement.document_title: ChatGPT and delusions: an important new inside look at OpenAI

from_speaker: at OpenAI, as described in the NYT inside report
our_interpretation: Plain reading: people inside OpenAI raised several warnings about risks of ChatGPT's behaviour to users (sycophancy, emotional dependence, harm to vulnerable users), and the company went ahead anyway or did not act on them.
'Lots' is read as more than one documented warning. It does not require a specific count.
The period is the history the NYT report covers, from 2020 to the post date.
criteria.support_condition: Credible reporting or OpenAI's own statements document multiple internal warnings about these risks that OpenAI overrode or did not act on.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The documented internal warnings were acted on, or there is no evidence of more than an isolated warning being disregarded.
